# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Taylor Ellison**
[Your street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Your phone number]

[Date of this letter]

Independence Blue Cross
The Member Appeals Department
P.O. Box 41820
Philadelphia, PA 19101-1820
Fax: 1-888-671-5274

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-02**
**Member:** Taylor Ellison
**Member ID:** W798611035
**Reference number:** POC-2FE0EDCD1B-73051
**Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Plan:** Independence Blue Cross (Commercial/ACA), Pennsylvania
**Governing policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines — Musculoskeletal: Joint Surgery (2025-11-15), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my total hip replacement (CPT 27130). The notice dated 2026-08-02 states that the request was denied because the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery. I am asking Independence Blue Cross to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Duval, MD, requested this procedure and has documented in my chart that it is needed.

I believe the records already in your possession show a long and thorough trial of conservative treatment, and that the decision can be corrected on review.

## A note about the criteria I was given

I want to be straightforward with your reviewer about one thing. The criteria language I received in connection with this denial, and that I am able to quote, comes from the shoulder arthroplasty sections of the governing guideline. For example, the plan's policy states:

> "shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:"

and, within that same section:

> "Irregular joint surfaces Glenoid sclerosis Osteophyte changes Flattened glenoid Cystic changes in the humeral head Failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks' duration (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 or diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III-IV changes) Hemiarthroplasty Hemiarthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications:"

My surgery is a hip replacement, not a shoulder procedure. No hip-specific criterion from the plan's policy has been quoted to me, so the rest of this letter makes its argument in my own words rather than by quoting policy language I have not been given. If Independence Blue Cross is relying on a hip-specific conservative-care requirement within the Carelon Musculoskeletal: Joint Surgery guideline, I respectfully ask that the exact language be identified in the appeal response so that it can be compared directly to my records.

I would also point out that the only conservative-management threshold in the language I have been given is a failure of conservative management of at least 6 weeks' duration. My documented conservative care runs well past that length, as set out below.

## What my records show about conservative treatment

These facts come from the prior authorization packet already submitted on my behalf:

- **Duration of symptoms:** 18 months of progressive pain in the hip, unrelieved by rest.
- **Supervised physical therapy:** 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, from 2026-02-20 to 2026-06-12, with 16 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication:** NSAIDs for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Injection:** A corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21, which gave 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging (2026-06-13):** Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph showing joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.
- **Examination:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.
- **Function:** I walk with a cane, I am limited to about one block, and I cannot put on my shoes unassisted.
- **Safety factors:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Taken together, these records document a four-month course of medication, a full 16-week supervised physical therapy program completed to discharge, and an injection that gave only two weeks of partial relief — all before surgery was requested, and all within an 18-month history of worsening pain. That is a trial of conservative treatment, and the records reflect that it did not work.

I would also note that the records show no active infection, which is relevant because the plan's policy lists as a contraindication:

> "Active infection of the joint Active systemic bacteremia Active skin infection or open wound at the surgical site Rapidly progressive neurologic disease Intra-articular corticosteroid injection within the past 6 weeks in the joint being replaced Exclusions Indications other than those addressed in this guideline are considered not medically necessary including, but not limited to, the following:"

None of those conditions appear in my chart.

## What I am requesting

I respectfully ask that Independence Blue Cross:

1. Overturn the denial issued 2026-08-02 (reference POC-2FE0EDCD1B-73051) and authorize total hip replacement, CPT 27130;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with experience in orthopedic surgery; and
3. If the denial is upheld, identify in writing the exact hip-specific criterion from the Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines — Musculoskeletal: Joint Surgery (2025-11-15) that my records are said not to meet, and state which specific records were reviewed.

I understand from the denial notice that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of that notice, by **2027-01-29**. I am submitting this letter to The Member Appeals Department, P.O. Box 41820, Philadelphia, PA 19101-1820, and it may also be submitted by fax to 1-888-671-5274 or by phone to 1-888-671-5276.

Enclosed with this letter are the supporting records: [list enclosures — e.g., physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-06-12, radiology report dated 2026-06-13, office notes from Duval, MD, medication records].

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I am happy to provide anything further that would help your reviewer.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Ellison**
Member ID: W798611035
[Your phone number]
[Your email address, if you wish to include one]

**Enclosures:** [list]
